steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Pound chicken breasts until thinned out. In a shallow dish or bowl mix together bread crumbs and cheese. Dip one side of each breast into melted butter or margarine, then into crumb/cheese mixture. Place a dollop of cheese spread at one end of each chicken breast, on the side of the breast not dipped in the mixture. Roll up each breast and secure with toothpicks.

Place rollups in a lightly greased 9x13 inch baking dish and drizzle any remaining butter or margarine over all. Bake in the preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes, or until cooked through and juices run clear.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic Cheese Chicken Rollups
raw_recipe.description: A Parmesan-butter crust encases chicken rolled around a dollop of garlic cheese.

review.reviewBody: I found this recipe to be absolutely amazing! I followed the recipe exactly, but with my own cheese spread. I added together a package of cream cheese, dry chives, minced garlic, garlic powder and onion powder and blended it in the food processor until wonderfully whipped. This is one of the best new recipes I've made in weeks. I highly recommend everyone try this at least once!

Delicious! I followed the revies and marinated the pounded out chicken breasts in Italian dressing and made my own cream cheese spread with my food processor. Since the breasts were already covered in dressing I just poured the butter on at the end and it worked fine. I used light cream cheese. Served this with brown rice and creamed peas and onions but I would recommend a lighter veg as the chicken was very rich. I will make these again and experiment with different seasonings.

Phenomenal! I made this for Christmas dinner and it was delicious. Took a reviewer's suggestion and marinated the chicken in the Kraft Zesty Dressing for about 2-3 hrs before. I used the Phildelphia whipped chive cream cheese for easier spreading and a mixture of Italian bread crumbs and panko to get a nice crunch on the chicken. I kept it in the oven for about 40-45min and it was great!

In Mexico so used cream cheese, fresh chives, fine chopped red onion, crushed fresh garlic and McCormick Chipotle Garlic Seasoning.
Added crushed chichorones (pork skins) to breading for crispness. 
After spreading mixture on chicken and rolling up, I refrigerated them to make easier to dip in butter and roll in breading. Excellent!

My boyfriend who doesn't like chicken breasts very much said I should make this again. That's definately a hit recipe! Per other reviews, I marinated the chicken in Italian Dressing for a few hours first. For the cheese I used Laughing Cow French Onion flavor (that's what was in the fridge) and did 1 triangle per chicken breast. The bread crumbs were Panko with seasonings added (red pepper, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper). Since I marinated it in dressing I skipped the butter except to spray the rolls with butter-flavored PAM before baking. My oven took a little longer so it was baked at 350 for 40 minutes and 375 for 7 minutes. Maybe the breasts were thicker? I will definately make this again and try different flavors of cheese spread.

You must try! I made these this week and they were delicious! I used recipe as a base recipe only and then modified to my liking. I pounded 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts between 2 pieces of wax paper til they were nice and thin. I then marinated them in ranch, basil, italian seasoning, pinch of cayanne, and a bit of olive oil for a few hours. I used melted butter to make the mix of bread crumbs and cracker crumbs stick to one side of each breast. Then I chopped garlic, jalapenos, and peanuts. I mixed these with sour cream, a pinch of cayanne, oregano, italian seasoning, and italian herb philly cooking cream. I spooned the filling into each breast and rolled up, securing with toothpicks. I put into a shallow baking dish and I used the remaining melted butter on top of each chicken roll, then added more crumbs. Baked at 350 degrees for 45 minutes. They came out perfect and crispy. My boyfriend loved them. I forgot the cheese but they still were fantastic. Quick and easy to prepare. Will definitely make again.

Great Recipe!! Made it for family that came over and everyone loved it! Followed some other's reviews and marinated the pounded chicken breasts in Zesty Italian dressing for about 1/2 hr., used the Alouette Garlic & Herb spreadable cheese and used Progresso Italian Panko breading with some extra parm cheese on top... turned out awesome!

This recipe was very easy and quick to prepare. It was delicious, too! Hubby raved about it! We used a garlic/herb cheese spread (from our grocery deli) and Italian-seasoned bread crumbs. We also sprinkled a little extra cheese over the top, just before baking. Served it with spicy green beans and buttered corn. Will be adding this to our regular roation of meals!

Lots of flavor! I used many of the suggestions made by others. I marinated the chicken breasts in Zesty Italian Dressing for a few hours before preparation. I found a cheese spread by Alouette called Garlic and Herbs. I also used an Italian seasoned bread crumb mixture with the parmesan. Prior to putting the mix in the oven, I topped each breast with marinara. I baked the chicken for around 30 minutes, then added a thin sprinkling of mozzarella cheese. I baked for an additional 10 minutes. Very tender and very tasty.

LOVED it! I made 8 breasts with the same amount of ingredients and I didn't skimp at all on the mixture. I think if you were going to only do 4, you really could use 1/2 cup of bread crumbs. I used the Itailian bread crumbs in mine, I didn't have to use much of the garlic cheese spread. I found the cheese spread in the cheese case (not with all the prepackaged stuff) and a small teaspoon is plenty! I also sprinkled some leftover bread crumb mixture on the top of each piece of chicken and then topped it off with a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese. I didn't use the prepackaged parmesan cheese, I purchased the grated real stuff! VERY, VERY GOOD!!!

I made this tonight but made my own garlic cheese spread with 4 oz crm cheese, 1/4c parm cheese,1/4 C minced red bell pepper,parsley for color. For the breadcrumb substitute I used panko crumbs with basil,salt n pepper,and 1/8 tsp of dill. Seved it with mashed potatoes, and buttered corn. Nice change to basic stuffed chix breast like cordon blue,kiev, and reg stuffing. Thank you
This is terrific. I found the garlic cheese spread in the deli section of my local Giant. Boursin brand.

Made for my grandsons who are picky eaters but love fried chicken and cheese. These are easy to make - a tad messy but easy. They inhaled them. I thought they came out good too but had problems keeping the cream cheese inside. It kind of spilled out during the baking process but still tasted great.
I didn’t make any real changes, but you can get away with using half of the cheese and bread crumb mixture. I had a lot leftover. I will make it again.
Delicious w soft garlic cheese spread. Could use cr ch instead.

Was delicious! Husband, who is the cook in the family loved it and I made it lol. Does need a lot more butter to dip in before bread crumbs, I also added salt and pepper inside the chicken before rolling with the cheese. I used the laughing cow creamy Swiss garlic & herb wedges, however I think next time I will make my own with cream cheese. I thought it needed more salt but I’m also a salt addict so… Overall it was a wonderful dish and I will be making it again!
I used crushed Ritz crackers and a spinach artichoke dip that was leftover from a party. Wow was it good!

Tasty chicken breast dish. I used the remaining breadcrumb/cheese mixture and sprinkled it all over the chicken before cooking. I also added a little rosemary and thyme into the mix. 
Cooking time was approx. 45 minutes
Delicious!
